quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: As a beginning rider, what should you do when following another vehicle?

options.text: Keep at least a four-second distance behind the vehicle.
Get as close to the vehicle as possible.
Do not worry about following distance.
Always ride on the left side of the lane so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep at least a four-second distance behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least a four-second gap between their motorcycle and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if road or weather conditions are poor.

questions.question: Which of these should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Help you avoid hazards on the road.
Give you a way to escape danger.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position keeps you out of other vehicles' blind spots, helps you see and be seen, helps you avoid road hazards, protects you from wind blasts, and gives you an escape route. Your position should discourage other drivers from entering your lane.

questions.question: Why should cargo be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load might block the turn signals.
You may not be able to see over a high load.
Other drivers cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Placing cargo too high on a motorcycle raises its center of gravity and makes the motorcycle harder to balance.

questions.question: What can help reduce your chances of a crash?

options.text: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Do not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible, communicate your intentions, maintain safe distance, look ahead 12 seconds or more, identify hazards early, and be ready for changing conditions.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
About 95 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake using only the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop as fast as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake using only the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and keep your course straight. If you must brake, gradually use the brake of the good tire. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, pull in the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Read books about carrying passengers.
Practice riding on a quiet road.
Flash your lights to show other drivers you are there.
Practice riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger or heavy cargo in traffic for the first time, practice on a quiet road to get used to how the extra weight changes how your motorcycle handles.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about hazards or conditions ahead.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: You may lose traction on one or both wheels.
You may stop sooner than expected.
You may pop a tire.
It may take longer to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may lose traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can cause you to lose traction on one or both wheels, which can lead to a crash.

questions.question: When approaching an object or uneven surface you cannot avoid, what should you do?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up.
Swerve quickly.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible. Slow down as much as you can. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off the seat so your knees absorb some of the impact. Just before you hit it, gently roll on the throttle to lighten the front tire.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Apply the brake on the tire that is flat.
Apply both brakes.
Do not use either brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, gradually apply the brake on the tire that is not flat, if you know which one that is.

questions.question: In a crash, which of the following does NOT help prevent serious injury?

options.text: Wear an approved helmet.
Wear face or eye protection.
Wear protective clothing.
Have a windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a windshield.
questions.explanation: To reduce injury risk, wear an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing. A windshield is not necessary for injury prevention.

questions.question: In group riding, what does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Danger ahead.
Stop.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with palm facing back, all riders in the group should stop.

questions.question: Motorists entering the highway from a ramp on your right may not see your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Flash your lights.
Move to the left side of your lane to share it if needed.
Move to another lane if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of space to vehicles entering the highway. Move to a lane away from the entrance ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give the vehicle room to safely enter.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When the pavement is dry.
When the pavement is wet.
When you can see through the vehicle ahead.
When the sun is out.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more distance to stop. Wet pavement, poor visibility, or heavy traffic all require more space between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The horn may go off.
Your motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and a warning light will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid, causing you to lose control. Always slow down enough before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve what?

options.text: Speeds greater than 35 mph.
Worn tires.
Riding in the dark.
Inexperienced riders on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inexperienced riders on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders with little experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Roll on the throttle.
Hold the handlegrips loosely.
Gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to exit the road faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and stay in a straight line as you slow down. If you must brake, gradually apply the brake on the tire that is not flat, if you know which one that is.

questions.question: Which provides the best face protection?

options.text: Sunglasses
Windshield
Goggles
Face shield

questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not provide adequate face protection.

questions.question: During your pre-ride inspection, what should you NOT check?

options.text: Fluids.
Headlight and taillight.
Turn signals.
Reflectors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflectors.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil, fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: Before riding, what should you NOT check?

options.text: Your tire pressure.
The tread on your tires.
How reflective your tires are.
The condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.correctAnswerText: How reflective your tires are.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tire tread wear, and the condition of the sidewalls and tread surface.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you as easily as other vehicles.
Assume other drivers cannot see you.
Not worry about whether other drivers see you.
Ride aggressively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than other vehicles, making them hard to see. Ride defensively and assume other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: If one rider in a group wants to ride faster than the others, what should the group do?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a designated spot later.
Speed up to match that rider's speed.
Split up so each rider can go at their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a designated spot later.
questions.explanation: If one group member wants to ride faster, let them go ahead and meet the group at a designated location.

questions.question: Engine braking:

options.text: Is illegal.
Means turning off the engine to slow down.
Means slowing down by downshifting.
Is not recommended because it damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Means slowing down by downshifting.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows the motorcycle like using the brakes. This is called engine braking.
